title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners
version_designed_for: NARROWER NON-VENTURE VERSION named in G34-score.json (verdict: KILL as a venture; best-available bootstrappable path). Designed here: an open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema plus a TAK Server-side extension that stores ICS 201/204/209/214 and a resource/status ledger (the civil analogue of LOGSTAT) as CRDT-merged mission objects, with an ATAK-CIV plugin, a thin iOS companion app (iTAK accepts no plugins) and a web companion for the incident command post, transported over TAK Server Data Sync missions, FirstNet/LTE and Meshtastic LoRa. Stewarded with the TAK Public Safety community and WFTAK; monetised only through hosting, support and training to state wildland agencies and incident management teams. The Guard variant is kept ONLY as a no-cost drill-weekend probe of willingness to pay (no program office exists), the allied variant is deferred to a possible NATO DIANA 2028 application, and the 'license the merge model to HQ/C2 platform owners' line is DROPPED (CRDT engines are open source; Ditto already sells CRDT sync for ATAK). Every milestone below tests the decisive doubt: does any named agency, IMT, Guard unit or platform owner pay for this rather than use free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS? This is an open-source-plus-services or acquihire path, not a venture-scale company, and the plan is written so the founders can kill it cheaply.

architecture.prose: INPUTS. Structured entries typed by the planning section (ICS 201 briefing, 202 objectives, 204 assignment lists, 209 status summary, 214 unit log) and by field elements (division/group status, resource check-in, quantities of crews/engines/water/fuel, the civil analogue of a LOGSTAT); ATAK position (PLI) and map markers already flowing as Cursor-on-Target (CoT); CSV/PDF exports from an existing IMS (WebEOC, Tablet Command, Intterra) or from the interagency resource ordering system where an MOU allows; and public incident data (perimeters, weather) used only as demo context. COMPUTE. Commercial Android end-user devices running ATAK-CIV with the plugin; iOS phones/tablets running a native companion app (because iTAK has no third-party plugin model, FACT from the Meshtastic 2026-02 blog in G34 evidence); a command-post laptop or small server running TAK Server (open source, GPLv3, FACT from the TAK-Product-Center/Server LICENSE.md fetched 2026-09-25) with the structured-objects extension, or OpenTAKServer where an agency prefers it; an optional hosted multi-tenant instance for agencies without IT staff. CORE SOFTWARE. (1) A public JSON schema for ICS objects (form, field, list-of-assignments, resource ledger entries) versioned and published under Apache-2.0 so TPC, IMS vendors and the community can adopt it; (2) a CRDT document per incident built on Automerge (MIT; 3.0 in 2025 cut memory 10x, FACT per BigGo 2025-08) or Loro (MIT; smaller encodings per loro.dev benchmarks) with a form-tuned merge policy: per-field last-writer-wins with causal history for text, add-wins list/set merges for assignment rosters, and a counter/ledger discipline for quantities in which each node records signed deltas against a named resource rather than overwriting totals, so a partition never silently double-subtracts; (3) an explicit conflict surface that flags any quantity or assignment where two nodes made incompatible decisions (same crew assigned to two divisions) for a human to resolve; (4) a compact delta codec (protobuf, ~100-300 bytes per field edit) with store-and-forward queueing sized for LoRa; (5) a form renderer and PDF exporter producing the standard FEMA ICS form layouts (NIMS ICS Forms Booklet, public) so the paper-era workflow is preserved; (6) an audit/history view (who changed what, when, from which node) that doubles as the ICS 214 unit log. INTERFACES. TAK Server Mission API / Data Sync (missions hold CoT, files, logs and change feeds and re-sync data missed while disconnected, FACT per TAK Server README and OpenTAKServer docs): the extension stores each CRDT change as a mission content item so any TAK Server, including government ones the team never touches, can carry the deltas; CoT XML/protobuf for map overlays of assignments (division boundaries, resource icons); the ATAK-CIV plugin SDK 5.5 (Jetpack Compose support, FACT per RIIS blog 2026) for the Android UI; the Meshtastic protobuf/ATAK-forwarder path for LoRa transport between nodes with no server reachable (peer-to-peer CRDT gossip); EDXL-SitRep 1.0 (OASIS, 2013) export, which already maps ICS-201/203/207/209/215 (FACT per OASIS docs), for handoff to WebEOC-class systems; REST/WebSocket for the iOS and web companions. OUTPUTS. The next operational period's ICS 204s and the incident's 209 generated from merged objects; a resource status board; PDF/printed forms; a TAK map overlay of assignments; an EDXL-SitRep/CSV handoff to the agency's existing IMS. USER. Incident commander, planning section chief, resource unit leader and division supervisors on a Type 1-4 incident; the equivalent staff on a Guard drill weekend (S3/S4/battle captain) as a probe; later, a state wildland agency technology lead as the buyer of hosting/support.

architecture.hardest_problem: Not the CRDT algorithm (commodity) but the FORM SEMANTICS of merge under partition: ICS assignments and quantities are decisions, not text, so a mathematically correct merge can be operationally wrong (two divisions each 'take' the last engine; a crew is on two 204s; a 209 total is summed from stale ledgers). The hard engineering is (a) a schema and merge policy in which quantities are ledgers of signed deltas with causal context, assignments are add-wins sets with uniqueness invariants, and every invariant violation is surfaced to a named role rather than auto-resolved; (b) making that policy identical across three code bases (Kotlin plugin, Swift companion, TypeScript web) with a shared Rust/WASM core so behaviour never diverges; and (c) carrying the deltas across heterogeneous transports (TAK mission sync via server, peer-to-peer LoRa with ~200-byte packets and loss, LTE) with idempotent, reorderable application and bounded queue growth over a 6-12 hour partition. The demo must show convergence and correct conflict surfacing on all three platforms simultaneously; that is where prior tools (queue-and-replay IMS, Data Sync missions) stop.

must_be_proprietary: Honest answer: almost nothing can be proprietary and the score file says so. The only assets worth holding back from open source are (1) the hosted multi-tenant service, its tenancy/security hardening and GovRAMP artifacts, (2) the agency-specific import/export adapters (WebEOC, Tablet Command, state resource systems) built under paid pilots, and (3) training curricula and exercise playbooks. The schema, merge policy and reference clients should be open source (Apache-2.0 for the schema and core, matching the community-steward strategy); keeping them closed would remove the only plausible adoption lever (TAK Public Safety/WFTAK stewardship) without creating a moat.

architecture.integration_burden: Medium for the demo, high for revenue. Demo: one TAK Server with the extension, one ATAK plugin, one iOS app, one web page and Meshtastic nodes - all interfaces are documented and open, so two founders plus one iOS contractor can integrate them in 3-5 months. Revenue: every paying agency has a different IMS (WebEOC, Tablet Command, Intterra, Veoci; DHS SAVER 2022 lists 10+), different resource-ordering exports, different device policies (MDM, iOS majority) and different security reviews; each adds 2-6 weeks of adapter and onboarding work, which is services revenue, not product. Military probe: a Guard drill weekend on TAK-CIV/Data Sync needs no ATO for a demo but any persistent Guard use would require TAK-GOV builds, Army network ATO and possibly CUI handling, which this team should not take on. Platform-owner licensing integrations (Onebrief, Lattice, SitaWare) are closed APIs and are out of scope for this version.

performance_metrics.metric: Convergence time after reconnect (all nodes show identical merged state)
performance_metrics.target: < 30 s over LTE/FirstNet; < 10 min over a 3-hop Meshtastic LoRa mesh for a 6-hour partition of ~50 objects and ~500 field edits
performance_metrics.why: The failure mode being sold against is divergent pictures after partition; the planning section must trust that the board is current before the next briefing (operational periods are typically 12 h)

performance_metrics.target: 0 of N concurrent edits lost across Android, iOS and web in every test run
performance_metrics.why: One lost assignment or quantity destroys trust in the tool and sends staff back to paper

performance_metrics.target: 100% of true invariant violations (double-assigned crew, over-allocated resource) flagged; < 5% false flags
performance_metrics.why: Silent auto-merge of decisions is the specific weakness of generic CRDTs; false flags waste the IC's attention

performance_metrics.metric: Bytes per edit on the wire
performance_metrics.target: median < 200 bytes per field edit; full ICS 204 < 4 KB compressed; full incident snapshot < 100 KB
performance_metrics.why: Meshtastic packets are ~200-230 bytes payload and LoRa airtime is duty-cycle limited; FirstNet is not the constraint

performance_metrics.target: >= 72 h fully disconnected local operation with bounded queue growth (< 5 MB/day/device)
performance_metrics.why: Wildland divisions and displaced command posts can be off-network for days

performance_metrics.metric: Time to produce next operational period's ICS 204s

performance_metrics.why: This is the pain agencies feel every period; the partition case is episodic

performance_metrics.target: 100% of object types viewable and editable on iOS companion

performance_metrics.target: < 3% additional drain per hour with sync active

mvp.demo: A 'partition-and-merge' exercise on commercial hardware: five field devices (three Android with ATAK-CIV plugin, two iOS with the companion app) and one command-post laptop running TAK Server plus the structured-objects extension, all seeded with a synthetic Type 3 wildland incident (public perimeter data, fictional resources). The command post publishes ICS 202 objectives and ICS 204s for operational period 1. Networks are then deliberately cut: two devices continue on Meshtastic LoRa only, two go fully dark, the laptop 'displaces' (restarts on a second machine restoring from local state). For 6 simulated hours every node edits the same assignments, check-ins and quantities (crews moved between divisions, engines reassigned, water and fuel consumed, a 214 log kept on each device). On reconnect the observer measures convergence time, bytes transferred, lost updates (must be zero) and the conflict queue (which must contain exactly the double-assignment and over-allocation cases scripted into the scenario). The planning section then generates operational period 2's ICS 204s and the 209 from the merged state, timed against a control group doing the same on paper/Word. The same engine is shown a second time with FRAGO/SITREP templates for a Guard S3 on a drill weekend, purely to ask whether anyone there would pay.
must_prove: Multi-writer edits to assignments, check-ins and quantities made during a 6-hour partition merge with zero lost updates and no duplicates on Android, iOS and web simultaneously (technical doubt)
Decision conflicts (same crew on two 204s, over-allocated resource) are surfaced, not silently merged, and are resolved by the resource unit leader in under a minute each (semantic doubt)
Deltas fit LoRa: a 6-hour partition of realistic edits syncs over a Meshtastic-only path within 10 minutes (transport doubt)
The next period's ICS 204s and 209 are produced at least 40% faster than the paper/Word control with fewer transcription errors (value doubt)

DECISIVE: at least one named agency, IMT or Guard unit with a budget line or purchasing vehicle states in writing that it would pay (LOI or purchase intent for a paid pilot of at least $10k) rather than use free TAK Data Sync plus its existing IMS; and TPC/TAK Public Safety do not signal that form objects are coming natively (market doubt - this is what the kill verdict rests on)

build_plan.work: Customer discovery in parallel with architecture: 10-15 interviews (IMT planning section chiefs, state wildland technology leads incl. WFTAK/Colorado CoE, TAK Public Safety board, two municipal fire TAK users, one Guard S3, one IMS vendor). Choose CRDT engine (Automerge vs Loro) by benchmarking encoded delta size for ICS 204 edits; publish v0.1 ICS object JSON schema (201/204/209/214 + resource ledger) on GitHub under Apache-2.0; stand up TAK Server + OpenTAKServer test rigs; write the partition test harness (scripted edit streams, network cut/restore, metrics capture).

Core: Rust/WASM merge core with form-tuned policy (LWW text, add-wins assignment sets, signed-delta quantity ledger, invariant checker producing a conflict queue); protobuf delta codec; TAK Server-side structured-objects service writing deltas as mission content and consuming the mission change feed. Web companion (TypeScript) for the command post with 204/209 rendering and PDF export. Start iOS contractor on the Swift companion against the REST/WebSocket API.

ATAK-CIV plugin (SDK 5.5, Compose UI) with offline local store, mission-content sync and CoT overlay of assignments; Meshtastic transport path (delta fragmentation, ack/idempotent apply, gossip between nodes with no server). First end-to-end partition test on three Android + web; fix convergence and queue-growth issues; measure bytes per edit against the < 200-byte target.

iOS companion reaches parity for all object types; full five-device + displacement test run three times with metrics recorded; conflict-surfacing accuracy tuned on scripted double-assignment cases; ICS 214 audit view; EDXL-SitRep export of 201/209. Advisor review of form fidelity against the FEMA booklet. Package: install guide (< 15 min target), TAK Server docker image, TAK.gov CIV plugin submission prepared.

Field demo #1 at a state wildland exercise, IMT training or TAK Public Safety event under MOU, with a paper/Word control group timed on producing the next period's 204s; collect written feedback and the decisive question: who would pay, from which line, via which vehicle. Optional Guard drill-weekend probe with FRAGO/SITREP templates on synthetic data only.

Decision month: compile evidence against kill criteria; if at least one paid-pilot commitment exists, scope the hosted tier and GovRAMP Snapshot/Core self-assessment and apply for the TAK.gov plugin listing; if none exists, hand the schema and reference implementation to TAK Public Safety/WFTAK as open source and stop, or pursue acquihire conversations (Ditto, TPC contractors, IMS vendors) with the demo as the asset.

kill_criteria: By end of month 6, no named agency, IMT or Guard unit with identified budget authority has committed in writing to a paid pilot of at least $10,000 or signed an LOI for a hosting/support subscription (the decisive market test)

Fewer than 4 of 12+ discovery interviewees rank 'picture diverges after disconnect / re-keying forms each period' among their top three operational pains, or most say free TAK Data Sync plus their existing IMS is sufficient
TPC, WFTAK or an IMS vendor (Tablet Command, Intterra, Resgrid) publicly announces or ships structured ICS objects with multi-writer offline merge before month 6
iOS companion cannot reach object-type parity within the $30k contractor budget, leaving the iOS-majority wildland user base unreachable
Technical targets missed after two fix cycles: any lost update in the five-device test, convergence over LoRa > 30 min for the 6-hour scenario, or conflict false-flag rate > 15%
The exercise control group produces period-2 forms as fast as the tool (no measured time saving), indicating the value is in the partition case only, which is too episodic to sell
Counsel advises the product or its intended Guard/allied use cannot be kept within EAR jurisdiction without excluding the non-U.S.-person founder from core development

stages.evidence_produced: ARR and retention; schema adoption by third parties; GovRAMP Authorized status; audited financials showing product vs services mix

capital_map.does_250k_reach_next_fundable_milestone: Yes for the bootstrapping milestone, no for a venture milestone. $250k covers Stage 0 ($6-20k), Stage 1 ($55-100k) and most or all of Stage 2 ($110-240k) at the low-to-mid assumptions, i.e., a working three-platform partition-and-merge MVP, a live exercise with a named agency and the decisive answer on willingness to pay, with $20-80k of headroom if founders take minimal stipends. It does NOT reach the milestone that the score file says would justify $2-5M of venture capital (20+ paying agencies or a state enterprise contract plus a licensing/integration LOI from a platform owner), and this analysis agrees that milestone is unlikely to be reached at all because the licensing buyer has no reason to pay for an open-source merge model and agency ACVs are too small to fund a sales team. The realistic 'next fundable' events after $250k are: (a) a state or multi-agency hosting/support contract that funds Stage 3 from revenue (bootstrapping), (b) a DHS S&T or NSF-style non-dilutive award only if the cap table is restructured to pass the >50% U.S.-person ownership test (needs counsel), or (c) an acquihire. Founders should treat $250k as the budget to get a clean yes/no by month 9-11, not as seed capital for a company.
capital_map.next_milestone: Stage 2 exit: a live exercise with a named state wildland agency or IMT showing >= 40% faster period-2 ICS 204 production with zero re-keying across Android/iOS/web after a 6-hour partition, plus at least one signed paid pilot (>= $10k) or state-level hosting/support LOI naming the budget line and vehicle, plus a written position from TPC/WFTAK on whether native form objects are planned
capital_map.assumptions: All figures are analyst estimates (HYPOTHESIS, LOW-MEDIUM confidence) for a software-only, unclassified, EAR-jurisdiction (EAR99 or 5D002/ENC per E07-F32, counsel to confirm) product with no SBIR, no ATO and no CUI in Stages 0-2. Hardware prices for LoRa nodes are FACT from June 2026 price surveys; EUD prices are RECALL not re-verified. GovRAMP/StateRAMP cost figures are ranges because the program publishes tiers (Snapshot/Core without 3PAO; Ready/Authorized with 3PAO) but not fixed prices (FACT per GovRAMP FAQ and consultancy guides, 2025-2026). Guard and allied lines are probes only; if either is pursued seriously, compliance and legal lines roughly double (TAK-GOV gating, Army network ATO, ITAR defense-service review per E07-F15) and the non-U.S.-person founder's role would need counsel. Salaries assume founders and early hires accept below-market pay; market-rate salaries raise Stage 3-4 by 40-60%.

first_five_hires.role: Fractional public-safety domain lead: retired Type 1/2 IMT planning section chief or state wildland fire technology lead (advisor at Stage 0-1, part-time employee at Stage 2)
first_five_hires.why: ICS form workflow, operational-period rhythm, exercise access and agency purchasing are tacit; the G34 record marks this fatal-if-absent and neither founder has it
first_five_hires.when: Month 1 as paid advisor; part-time from month 5

first_five_hires.role: iOS/Swift mobile engineer (contract first, then hire if pilots convert)
first_five_hires.why: iTAK has no plugin model and ~80% of wildland responders use iOS; without a native companion the product cannot be adopted by an IMT
first_five_hires.when: Month 2 contract; full-time only after first paid pilot

first_five_hires.role: SLED/public-safety sales and customer-success lead with fire-service references
first_five_hires.why: Public-safety buying runs on references, conferences, cooperative contracts and grant cycles; two students have none; this hire is also the test of whether ACVs can carry a salesperson
first_five_hires.when: Only after 2-3 paid pilots (Stage 3, month 12-18); earlier is cash burn without product-market evidence

first_five_hires.role: DevSecOps/compliance engineer (GovRAMP, state security reviews, SBOM, signing)
first_five_hires.why: Hosted tier sales to states stall on security questionnaires and GovRAMP Ready; founders should not spend their time on control narratives

first_five_hires.role: TAK trainer / community lead (ideally from the TAK Public Safety or CivTAK community)
first_five_hires.why: TAK Public Safety's charter says adoption is gated by training and community, not features; onboarding time is the real competitor

fatal_if_absent: Incident-command / fire-service domain expertise (planning section chief level) - without it the forms are mis-modelled and no agency trusts the tool
iOS mobile engineering - without a native companion the iOS-majority user base is unreachable and the product is Android-only

Offline-first distributed-systems engineering (CRDT semantics, transport idempotence) - the engineer founder must own this personally; it cannot be outsourced without losing the only technical differentiator
SLED/public-safety sales capability with references by Stage 3 - absent, the company is an open-source project, not a business (acceptable outcome, but must be recognised)

engineering_risks.risk: Generic CRDT merge silently produces operationally wrong results for decisions and quantities (double-assigned crews, over-allocated resources, stale totals)
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design the schema as ledgers and sets with explicit invariants; the demo scripts these exact cases and must show them in the conflict queue, not auto-resolved; measure false-flag rate

engineering_risks.risk: Three code bases (Kotlin plugin, Swift companion, TypeScript web) diverge in merge behaviour
engineering_risks.mitigation: Single Rust core compiled to JNI/WASM/Swift bindings; a shared conformance test suite of recorded partition scenarios run in CI against all three; the demo runs all three platforms simultaneously

engineering_risks.risk: Deltas do not fit LoRa packet and duty-cycle limits, so the Meshtastic path is unusable for real incident volumes
engineering_risks.mitigation: Benchmark Automerge vs Loro encodings in month 1; fragment and prioritise (assignments and quantities before free text); the demo measures bytes per edit and LoRa-only convergence for a 6-hour scenario; if it fails, restrict LoRa to status/quantity objects and rely on FirstNet for text

engineering_risks.risk: TAK Server Mission API or ATAK plugin API changes across releases break the extension
engineering_risks.mitigation: Store deltas as opaque mission content (the most stable primitive), test against TAK Server and OpenTAKServer in CI, and keep a server-independent peer path; budget one maintenance sprint per ATAK release

engineering_risks.risk: GPLv3 copyleft on TAK Server entangles the extension or the hosted service
engineering_risks.mitigation: Run the structured-objects service as a separate process using the public Mission API; get written counsel on the boundary in Stage 1; publish the core as Apache-2.0 anyway since openness is the adoption strategy

engineering_risks.risk: iOS App Store review or MDM policies block the companion app or its background sync
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design for foreground sync with push-to-refresh plus a background-fetch budget; use standard location permissions; test with one agency's MDM early; keep the web companion as the fallback for iPads

engineering_risks.risk: Agencies store responder PII and location, triggering security reviews and CJIS-adjacent expectations the founders cannot meet
engineering_risks.mitigation: Minimise PII in the schema (roles and resource IDs, not personal data), encrypt at rest, offer on-prem TAK Server deployment as the default and hosted only as the paid tier; GovRAMP Snapshot self-assessment in Stage 2

engineering_risks.risk: The value shows only in the partition case, which is episodic; day-to-day form production is no faster than paper
engineering_risks.mitigation: The exercise includes a timed control group on period-2 form production; if there is no measured saving the kill criterion fires and the schema is donated to the community

engineering_risks.risk: TPC adds form objects to Data Sync, or an IMS vendor adds offline multi-writer merge, during the build
engineering_risks.mitigation: Ask TPC and WFTAK directly in Stage 0 and record the answer; keep the build short (4 months) and open source so the outcome is still a usable community asset or acquihire portfolio, not a stranded product

engineering_risks.risk: Scope drift toward Guard/allied features pulls the codebase or the team's activities toward controlled technical data or ITAR 'defense services' (E07-F15) and complicates the non-U.S.-person founder's role
engineering_risks.mitigation: Keep the Guard drill weekend a synthetic-data probe on TAK-CIV only; no unit data, no TAK-GOV builds, no integration work for a foreign military without export-control counsel; document the EAR classification memo before any such contact
